ai.h1: Ask your ai to help with your documents.
ai.lede: Golem Docs has no ai of its own, on purpose. It keeps every document in a folder on your computer, and an ai app that can work in a folder can read your documents, tidy them up and write new ones, while you keep working in Golem Docs.
ai.step1.h: Install Golem Docs on your computer.
ai.step1.p: It’s free, for Mac, Windows and Linux. Download it.
ai.step2.h: Choose a folder for your documents.
ai.step2.p: Golem Docs asks the first time it opens, and File › Vault Folder changes it later. Your documents appear there as ordinary files.
ai.step3.h: Open that folder in your ai app.
ai.step3.p: Each ai app does this a little differently. Here is how in four of them.
ai.claude.1: In the message box, choose Cowork.
ai.claude.2: Click +, add a folder, and pick your Golem Docs folder.
ai.claude.3: Ask away. Keep the app open while it works on your files.
ai.claude.note: Cowork is in beta on Mac, Windows and Linux, on paid Claude plans.
ai.chatgpt.2: Open a local folder and pick your Golem Docs folder.
ai.chatgpt.3: Ask away. It asks before changing anything outside that folder.
ai.chatgpt.note: Mac and Windows. Local folders only work in the desktop app, not on the web or your phone.
ai.cli.1: In a terminal, go to your Golem Docs folder.
ai.cli.3: Or, in the Codex app, choose the folder as your project and pick Local.
ai.cli.note: Both read the AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) at the top of the folder. More on the developers page.
ai.cursor.1: Choose File › Open Folder and pick your Golem Docs folder.
ai.cursor.3: Look over its changes before you keep them.
ai.cursor.note: Cursor is made for code, but it works on any folder of files.
ai.apps.note: Menus change as these apps are updated; if a step looks different, look for the option to open or add a folder.
ai.ask1: “Turn my meeting notes into a one-page summary for Sam.”
ai.ask2: “Find every recipe that uses basil and list them in a new note.”
ai.ask3: “Fix the spelling in my cover letter, but don’t change my wording.”
ai.ask4: “Make a table from this year’s running log.”
ai.asks.balloon: It works on Word files, PDFs and drawings too, not only notes.
ai.how.p: Golem Docs keeps the folder and your account in step. A change on either side reaches the other, and from there your browser, your other devices and anyone you share a document with.
sync.note: Keeping the folder in step with your account, and through it your other devices and the people you share with, comes with sync, $3 a month. Without it, the folder and Golem Docs still keep in step on this computer, and versions and the trash are kept on it. On the same computer, a change in the folder shows up in Golem Docs within a few seconds, and one made in Golem Docs reaches the folder within a minute. Other devices look at your account about once a minute.
ai.free.h: Or sync it yourself, for free
ai.free.p: You don’t need a subscription to use your documents on more than one computer. Put your Golem Docs folder in iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or Google Drive, and choose that same folder in Golem Docs on each computer. Your cloud drive carries the files between them, and your ai app can work on them from any of them. What you give up is sharing: editing a document with other people, live, needs sync.
ai.flow.label: Your ai app works in the documents folder on your computer, which syncs with your account, which reaches your other devices and the people you share with.
ai.undo.p: Letting an ai change your notes should not be scary. Golem Docs keeps earlier versions of every document, whoever changed it.
ai.undo.f1: Golem Docs keeps the version from before each burst of changes, and one every ten minutes while the changes go on. A change that cuts a document to less than half its size always keeps the one before it.
ai.undo.f2: A document that is deleted goes to the trash for 30 days.
ai.undo.f3: If ten or more files vanish at once, Golem Docs waits for you before it does anything. That is far more often an unplugged drive than a decision.
ai.undo.balloon: This is the history of one document. Open makes a new document from that version, so the one you have is left as it is.
ai.rules.h: Tell your ai how you like things kept
ai.rules.p: Most ai apps read a short note of instructions at the top of the folder before they start. Here is one to begin with; change it to suit you.
ai.rule1: Look for notes I already have before writing a new one, and add to them.
ai.rule2: Put each new note in the folder that fits it. Ask before making a new folder.
ai.rule3: Link new notes to related ones, and add them to the folder’s index.
ai.rule4: Keep my own writing in my voice. Add to it; don’t rewrite it.
ai.rules.note: Save it as a note named AGENTS.md in the folder. The file, ready to copy, is on the developers page.
ai.mine.p: My own folder, as it is today:
ai.mine.1: Diary, written in Golem Docs most mornings
ai.mine.2: AI Research, one folder per paper, with my notes and the PDF together
ai.mine.3: Books, a note for each book I read
ai.mine.balloon: When Claude looks something up for me, it saves the paper and its note here before it finishes.
ai.choice.p: Golem Docs never sends your documents to an ai. When you let an ai app work in your folder, what it reads goes to the company that runs it, under their terms. Choose one you trust, and tell it which folders to leave alone.

pricing.h1: Free to use. Paying covers my server bills.
pricing.lede: Editing runs on your own device, so it costs me nothing to give away. Sync and sharing need a server and storage, and that is what the subscription pays for.
pricing.why.p: Sync keeps your documents on my server so they follow you to any device. Sharing lets people edit together, live. What is left over lets me keep working on Golem Docs. Sign in with Google, Microsoft, GitHub or Apple to subscribe, and cancel any time.
pricing.free.h: Or bring your own cloud drive, for free
pricing.free.p: You don’t have to pay to use Golem Docs on more than one computer. Keep your Golem Docs folder in iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or Google Drive, choose it in Golem Docs on each computer, and your documents follow you with no account at all. The one thing you don’t get is sharing: editing with other people, live, needs the subscription. More about the folder.
pricing.storage.p: Version history uses whatever space your documents leave. When the account fills up, the oldest automatic versions make room first. Versions you name are kept.
pricing.shared.h: Opening what others share is free
pricing.shared.p: If a subscriber shares a document with you, you only need to sign in to open it, and to edit it if they let you.
pricing.cancel.p: Your documents stay on your device, and downloading a file, or all your files zipped, never needs an account or a subscription.
pricing.balloon: A subscription doesn’t buy a place in the feature queue. Free users ask too, and I read every request.
pricing.v1.p: I don’t sell your data and I don’t show ads.
pricing.v2.p: No analytics and no advertising trackers.
pricing.v3.p: Every document is a real file that belongs to you. File › Download All saves everything as one ZIP, any time.
pricing.legal: I wrote the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service to be read. They are short.

about.p1: Hi, I’m David. Obsidian runs my life, but PDFs kept getting in the way: I was always hunting for a tool to convert one or edit one. ZIP files made it more interesting, because an archive can hold anything, so an editor that opens one has to open whatever is inside. I thought it would be fun if it could open every kind of document there is, and I have been building toward that ever since.
about.b1: It opens War and Peace too, all 1,006 pages, and stays fast.
about.p2: There is no ai inside Golem Docs, on purpose. Every document is an ordinary file in a folder on your computer, so the ai you already use can read it, tidy it up and write new notes next to it. What it changes shows up in the app a few seconds later, and, with sync, on your other devices within about a minute.
about.b2: Golem Docs keeps earlier versions of every document, whoever changed it. How it works ›
about.p3: Much of the code was written with Claude, with me steering. I promise I could have written it myself, but it would have taken years.
about.requests.h: Missing something? Ask, and it goes in the app.
about.requests.p1: Golem Docs has no plugin store, and it won’t get one. Plugins made sense when a missing feature meant weeks of someone’s spare time. With ai helping me write code, a missing feature can just be built, so I build it into the app, with tests, instead of leaving you to find an add-on.
about.requests.p2: That keeps things simple. There’s no third-party code running next to your documents, a new feature looks and works like the rest of the app in all 11 languages, and when the app changes, the feature changes with it.
about.requests.p3: If there’s something you do in a document that Golem Docs can’t, or a file type it doesn’t open, tell me at david@golemdocs.com, or with Help › Send Feedback in the app. I can’t promise a date, but what people ask for often gets built first.
about.b3: What I build each week is in the Journal.

open-source.h1: All of Golem Docs is open source.
open-source.lede: The editor, the server behind sync and sharing, and the libraries that read and write each format. Read it, run your own copy, or build something new with it.
open-source.why.p1: I build software because I want people to use it. Open source is the best way I know to get Golem Docs to everyone who would like it, and to let them shape it, run it their own way, or build something of their own from it.
open-source.why.p2: It also means you don’t have to take my word for anything. Your documents are files on your computer, and you can read every line of code that touches them, the server that syncs them included.
open-source.why.p3: The app is free, with no account and no ads, and $3 a month pays for sync and sharing on my server. That subscription is also how you support the project.
open-source.balloon: If I ever stopped working on Golem Docs, the code would still be here, and so would your files.
open-source.use.1: Nothing to set up. Golem Docs is free in your browser and on your computer, with or without an account.
open-source.use.2: The whole app, sync and sharing included, runs on your own Cloudflare account. The README on GitHub walks through it.
open-source.use.3: The code that reads and writes .docx, .odt and PDF, lays out pages and merges live edits is MIT licensed. Use it in anything, including closed-source software.
open-source.use.4: The app and server are AGPL-3.0. Change them however you like. If you share a changed copy, or run one as a website for other people, share your changes under the same license.
open-source.use.5: Welcome, under your own name and logo. The Golem Docs name and logo stay with this project.
open-source.help.p1: Bug reports and ideas are welcome as GitHub issues, and you can also email me at david@golemdocs.com or use Help › Send Feedback. What people ask for often gets built first.
open-source.help.p2: Code is welcome too. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a small fix, so we can agree on the approach. The first time you send code, you’ll be asked to agree to a short contributor agreement: you keep the copyright in your work, and I can keep running the hosted version.
open-source.legal: The app and server are under the AGPL-3.0; the format, layout, editing and collaboration libraries under MIT. Fonts and spelling dictionaries keep their own licenses.
dev.h1: Plain files, and a sync you can reason about.
dev.lede: Every document is a real file, in its real format, in a folder you choose. Point Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or your own scripts at it. The demo on the home page has a terminal tab.
dev.folder.1: .docx, .md, .txt, .csv, .svg, .epub and .mhtml files stay what they are.
dev.folder.2: PDFs are written with their annotations, form fields and edits in them, and pictures with their layers drawn in.
dev.folder.3: Folders in Golem Docs are folders on disk. Move or rename a file and the document follows, history and all.
dev.folder.4: Names starting with a dot are skipped, so .git is left alone. .golemdocs/ holds the sync state; don’t edit it.
dev.sync.1: The file wins. If the account changed too, its copy is kept as a version first.
dev.sync.2: The document goes to the account’s trash for 30 days.
dev.sync.3h: A file was moved or renamed
dev.sync.3: Same bytes, new place: it stays one document, with its history.
dev.sync.4: The sync holds and asks. It’s usually a drive that isn’t mounted.
dev.sync.5: The folder is checked every 4 seconds, the account every minute.
dev.agents.p: Agents read an instructions file at the top of the folder. Here is a starting point; change it to suit how you file things.
dev.agents.md:
# This folder is my second brain

It is my Golem Docs folder: every file here is a document in my account,
and what you change here syncs to all my devices.

- Search the folder before you write about a topic, and build on the notes
  that are already there.
- Put each new note in the folder that fits its topic. List the folders
  first. Ask before creating a new top-level folder.
- Use [[wikilinks]] to related notes, and add new notes to the folder's
  index note.
- Keep my own notes in my voice. Add links or a line at the end; don't
  rewrite what I wrote.
- Never touch .golemdocs/.
